question.problem: Find the solutions of the equation $16{y}^{2}+4=0.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{y}^{2}+4 & =0 \\ 16{y}^{2} & =-4 \\ {y}^{2} & =-\frac{4}{16} \\ {y}^{2} & =-\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

By taking square root, we obtain:

$$
y=\pm \sqrt{-\frac{1}{4}}
$$

We now rewrite $y$ using the imaginary unit $\text{i}=\sqrt{-1}\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\pm \sqrt{-\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-1)} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{1}}{\sqrt{4}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{1}{2}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
